subject: Extension hosting API: namespace migration and compatibility guarantees
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@lodestar.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@lodestar.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Extension hosting API - namespace migration impact & ask

Hi Priyom,

Quick intro — I'm Amit on the integration team at Lodestar. We run an ISV connector that embeds Redwood's extension-hosting client into our deployment pipeline. Over the weekend we picked up the new SDK snapshot and found a breaking change: the public namespace for extension lifecycle hooks moved from redwood.extensions to redwood.hosting.extensions in the 2027.04 preview. That change causes our bundled adapter and static analyzers to fail at startup.

We understand refactors happen, but Lodestar has 26 customers running the connector in production and a rolling upgrade would be disruptive without a compatibility path. Could Redwood do one of the following:

- Provide a short-term compatibility shim in the SDK (redirect old namespace to new) for the 2027.04 line, or
- Publish a clear migration plan with timelines and a deprecation window (we need at least 12 weeks notice), and code samples for the new namespace.

I've attached a minimal patch proposal (lodestar-proposed-shim-spec-v1.pdf) showing how we expect a shim to behave and a csv with example API surface diff. Happy to jump on a call this week.

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Shah
Director, Integrations — Lodestar Analytics
From: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@lodestar.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Extension hosting API - namespace migration impact & ask

Thanks Amit — really useful signal and thanks for the patch proposal. Looping in Marissa and Vanessa since this touches partner-facing SDK guarantees and our extension runtime.

Quick answers:
- We can ship a compatibility shim for the 2027.04 hosted SDK; engineering needs to validate complexity but this is plausible as a short-term mitigation.
- We will not make any breaking changes without a documented deprecation window; I agree 12 weeks is reasonable for ISV adapters.

Action items from our side:
1) Engineering will triage the shim feasibility and ETA (Marissa),
2) Product will draft a migration timeline and public SDK policy blurb (Vanessa),
3) We'll schedule a 30m sync with Lodestar to walk through the patch and agree rollback/fallback behavior.

Can you share a bit more about how Lodestar bundles the SDK (tree-shaken vs single bundle) and whether you rely on any reflection/monkey-patch behavior? That will help us scope the shim.

Best,
Priyom Das
Sr. Partner Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@lodestar.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-26T08:39:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Extension hosting API - namespace migration impact & ask

Thanks for the quick reply. A few clarifications from our side:

- Lodestar ships a single UMD bundle that vendors Redwood's client (not tree-shaken). We perform a small post-build transform to inject our telemetry hooks, so we do rely on symbol names.
- The problematic call sites are: redwood.extensions.init and redwood.extensions.registerHostCallbacks. The shim in our patch simply forwards calls to the new namespace and preserves the old method signatures.

Attachment: lodestar-proposed-shim-spec-v1.pdf (contains example shim code and tests).

Proposed meeting windows (Pacific): 2027-04-27 09:30 or 2027-04-27 15:00. We prefer the morning.

— Sarah Collins
Lead Integration Engineer, Lodestar Analytics
From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, Amit Shah <amit@lodestar.ai>, Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@lodestar.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-28T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Extension hosting API - namespace migration impact & ask

Hi Amit / Sarah — thanks for the details and the spec. I triaged this with runtime and SDK eng:

- Short-term: we will accept Lodestar's shim approach as the compatibility behavior. Engineering has a small change (~12 LOC) to add a thin forwarding layer mapping redwood.extensions.* to redwood.hosting.extensions.*. We will ship it as a patch to the 2027.04 branch within 5 business days, gated by a quick test that exercises bundled UMD usage.
- Medium-term: Product will publish a formal deprecation policy page and a 12-week migration timeline for any public namespace moves. Vanessa will draft the wording and publish it to developer.redwood.ai.
- Next steps: Priyom please schedule the 30m sync for 2027-04-29 09:30 PT (we'll take the morning). Amit/Sarah please confirm and share the exact bundle hash you saw the error on so runtime can reproduce locally (ideally a small repro repo).

Attachments: redwood-api-diff-202704.csv (engineer notes).

Marissa Cole
Director, Developer Ecosystem | Redwood Inference
